_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: "The input" is the message input [data-testid="message-input"]; "the send button" is [data-testid="send-button"]; "the chevron" is the send options button [data-testid="send-options-button"]; "the thinking indicator" is [data-testid="agent-thinking"]; "the Stop button" is button[aria-label="Stop"]; "queued badges" are [data-testid="queued-badge"]. "Tap X" means a touch step "start" on X immediately followed by a touch step "end" (a tap, not a click). "Send X and wait for work" means: fill the input with X; the send button should become enabled (up to 5s); tap it; the thinking indicator should become visible (up to 30s). "Queue X" means: fill the input with X; the chevron should be enabled and visible (up to 5s each); tap it; the queue option [data-testid="queue-option"] should become visible (up to 5s); tap it. Every test starts: navigate to /c/queue and wait (up to 30s) for the input to be visible. A queued message's menu can cancel it. 1. Navigate to /c/queue and wait for the input. 2. Send "delay: 15" and wait for work. 3. Queue "echo: test cancel". 4. A queued badge should become visible (up to 10s). 5. Tap it. 6. The cancel item [data-testid="cancel-queued"] should become visible (up to 5s).
